original_value: Recent advancements and major breakthroughs in machine learning (ML) technologies in the past decade have made it possible to collect, analyze, and interpret an unprecedented amount of sensory information. A new era for “smart” sensor systems is emerging that changes the way that conventional sensor systems are used to understand the world. Smart sensor systems have taken advantage of classic and emerging ML algorithms and modern computer hardware to create sophisticated “smart” models that are tailored specifically for sensing applications and fusing diverse sensing modalities to gain a more holistic appreciation of the system being monitored. Herein, a review of the recent sensing applications, which harness ML enabled smart sensor systems, is presented. First well‐known ML algorithms implemented in smart sensor systems for practical sensing applications are discussed. Subsequent sections summarize the practical sensing applications under two major categories: physical and chemical sensing and visual imaging sensing describing how the sensor technologies are coupled with ML “smart” models and how these systems achieve practical benefits. Finally, an outlook on the current trajectory and challenges that will be faced by future smart sensing systems and the opportunities that may be unlocked is provided.

result.paraphrase: Recent progress and major breakthroughs in machine learning (ML) over the past decade have made it possible to collect, analyze, and interpret unprecedented amounts of sensory data. A new era of “smart” sensor systems is emerging, transforming how conventional sensors are used to understand the world. By leveraging classical and emerging ML algorithms along with modern computer hardware, smart sensor systems have produced sophisticated, task-specific “smart” models for sensing applications and for fusing diverse sensing modalities to gain a more holistic view of the monitored system. This review presents recent sensing applications that use ML-enabled smart sensor systems. It begins by discussing well-known ML algorithms implemented in smart sensor systems for practical sensing uses. The following sections summarize practical applications in two main categories—physical and chemical sensing, and visual imaging sensing—describing how the sensor technologies are coupled with ML “smart” models and how these systems deliver practical benefits. Finally, it offers an outlook on the current trajectory, the challenges future smart sensing systems will face, and the opportunities they may unlock.
